To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ML infill is a viable and often beneficial alternative to other imputation methods for missing data, and that supplementing imputes with support columns for presence of infill is beneficial to downstream model accuracy.

for the given benchmark data sets, ML infill was usually found to outperform other imputation scenarios in terms of downstream model performance, and that supplementing imputated data with support columns signaling infill was found to be generally beneficial to downstream model accuracy.

the practical question of how to impute missing data in a way that is most likely to benefit downstream model performance.

the problem of infilling missing values in data, and our contributions include the development of a missing data imputation platform, the Automunge library, and a series of validation experiments to demonstrate the efficacy of ML imputation for downstream model performance.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Automunge library is a useful tool for data preprocessing, and the ML infill imputation strategy can be recommended as the preferred default.

the Automunge library platform is an effective tool for preprocessing tabular data for downstream machine learning tasks, including a production friendly imputation implementation that bases imputations on a designated train partition, with the addition of an auto ML imputation model that is usually within noise of the best performing imputation scenario for both categoric and numeric features, and further that the inclusion of support columns signaling infill is usually beneficial to downstream performance.
Automunge is a mature, stable, and production ready platform for data science preprocessing, with the imputation module in particular being recommended for use in production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Automunge is an open source python library for data science with an extensive feature library for tabular data, and with a missing data imputation feature that can be used to prepare data sets for downstream learning.

we have developed a missing data imputation platform for tabular learning with a production friendly design for consistent imputation models across datasets, with an implementation that includes an extensive set of imputation scenarios, including "ML Infill" in which models for target features are trained from a partitioned extract of a training set, and a validation experiment that benchmarked imputation scenarios towards model performance for a set of benchmark datasets, in which it has been found that ML Infill outperformed for many scenarios,

Automunge can now be used to prepare data for tabular learning with missing data, in which it will automatically select the best imputation method for each feature based on the data type of the feature, and will also automatically select the best ML imputation model based on the data distribution of the feature.
The main takeaway from our work is that

missing data is a fundamental problem in the practice of machine learning, and that there exists a variety of imputation strategies, with a few being available in the Automung library platform, with ML infill being the default strategy.
missing data is not a problem to be avoided, but rather to be solved.

ML infill can be a viable option for infilling missing data in tabular learning, with a recommendation for supplementing imputated data with boolean integer support columns signaling presence or absence of infill.
